Alex.confusing: How the Hugged and Turkey effects interact with what each role reports. For example, my Owl saw no visitors at Casey, and I couldn't tell whether I'd been hugged or Casey was lying.
Alex.fun: Round 2, when Blair openly claimed Floofer and the table went after Blair. Working out who was lying from the egg counts was satisfying.
Alex.change: Tell players their own round-end tallies, or show a short log of who visited whom after each round. That would make the deduction easier to learn from.
Alex.regret: In round 3 I visited Casey and said I was probably hugged, which was true. I should have flagged Casey, who was the real Floofer, more strongly. I could have said that Casey's Hawk claim didn't fit my hugged report.

Blair.confusing: The dawn report's wording for Confused and Hugged was hard to act on, since I couldn't tell whether my hug on Alex made their Hawk egg count meaningful. Alex's +1 in round 2 stayed unexplained to me.
Blair.fun: Round 2 was tense: Alex's and Casey's Turkey/Hawk egg stories collided, and the table had to work out which egg came from which visit.
Blair.change: Make the egg source visible in dawn reports, such as which visitor laid each egg, so claims like Turkey and Hawk can be checked without guesswork.
Blair.regret: In round 3 I claimed Mouser and announced what I learned from my visit, which made me the obvious target right after Alex was winked. I'd stay quiet about my role and point suspicion at Casey, who was the other Meowfia, without naming my own visit.

Casey.confusing: How the Turkey's egg works. The egg goes to the visitor, and I briefly got that backwards in round 2 and accused Alex wrongly. Whether a Turkey can see who visited it was also unclear.
Casey.fun: Round 1, when the table saw the two Hawk claims clash and everyone converged on Finley. We banked a big score pile together.
Casey.change: Give the Turkey a dawn report of who visited it, or state the Turkey rule more plainly. Also show the leader's lead more clearly, since a 20-point gap decided the whole game after round 1.
Casey.regret: In round 3, as the Floofer, I claimed Hawk and named a visit target I hadn't made, then contradicted myself. I should have hugged someone else and claimed a vague role, or claimed Floofer-adjacent info that matched Ellis's Eagle list, so I wasn't caught changing my story.

Drew.confusing: The confused-report rule was hard to use: my own dawn report was wrong, and I couldn't tell whether other players' egg counts were reliable. Hugged visitors and Turkey payouts also took a lot of tracing.
Drew.fun: Round 3's Hawk-versus-Hawk dispute, where Casey's visit story kept shifting until Blair's Mouser wink fit the table's pattern, was the most engaging stretch.
Drew.change: I'd make it clearer when a Wink or death happens, and whether a dead player's throws still count toward the banked score. Knowing that would have simplified the endgame decisions.
Drew.regret: In round 2 I was the Sphinx, a Meowfia, and I threw my wild W6 at Blair, who was my own teammate. I would instead keep quiet on that throw and stop pushing the table toward Casey, a Farm player.

Ellis.confusing: The Turkey and Hawk egg direction caused real confusion at the table, and so did how Floofer hugs interact with other effects. Several players, me included, argued from wrong readings of who gets the egg.
Ellis.fun: Round 3, when I used my Eagle visit to catch Casey's changed story. Then the table converged on Blair after the Mouser claim and the Wink death.
Ellis.change: I'd make the score gap less snowball-prone. Alex and Casey led after round 1 and I could never really catch up. Banking big throws as a winning team dominates everything else.
Ellis.regret: In round 3 I threw at Blair and not at Casey, who was the second cat (Floofer). I called Casey's lie out early, but then I dropped it. Splitting my throw wouldn't have helped much, though, because Blair was also a cat. I'd also have pressed Alex harder in round 2, since Alex was the leader and I was the only one who could challenge them.

Finley.confusing: How Hawk and Eagle counts interact with hugs and Turkey eggs, since a visit can give or take an egg from someone other than the visitor. Two players claiming the same animal was hard to read without knowing who was lying.
Finley.fun: Round 2, when Alex's +1 looked like a Turkey egg and the table spent the day arguing over the Turkey, Owl, and Eagle counts.
Finley.change: Show each player's visit targets publicly at dawn, so the egg-count arguments could be settled without everyone having to trust a claim.
Finley.regret: I used my Mouser Wink on Blair, a Farm Falcon, on day 1 and then claimed Hawk, which contradicted Casey's real Hawk claim. Next time I would keep the Wink for a clearer target and hold my claim until the counts were checked.
